description: Open source repositories that are in scope for active bug bounty programs, ordered by newest stable release first.

repos.name: cloudflare/workerd
repos.description: Apache-2.0 licensed C++ JavaScript and WebAssembly server runtime built on V8 and Cap'n Proto; it is the same runtime core that powers Cloudflare Workers and Pages Functions in production, packaged for self-hosting and local development, and it is what wrangler and miniflare execute against. Releases are date-versioned as v1.YYYYMMDD.N and cut on most weekdays, with the matching workerd and @cloudflare/workers-types npm packages published within minutes of the GitHub release. In scope for Cloudflare's HackerOne bug bounty program as an enumerated SOURCE_CODE asset, https://github.com/cloudflare/workerd, which the HackerOne API reports with eligible_for_bounty=true, eligible_for_submission=true and critical maximum severity; Cloudflare additionally carries an org-wide https://github.com/cloudflare asset that is likewise bounty and submission eligible at critical severity. The material caveat is that eligibility in this program is decided per asset rather than inherited from the organization: the same structured scope list explicitly carries sibling Cloudflare repositories, among them vinext-private, cloudflare-os, moq-rs, recapn, computer, saffron and privacy-gateway-server-go, at eligible_for_bounty=false and eligible_for_submission=false, so a finding only pays when it lands on a repository that is itself flagged eligible, and workerd is. Latest stable release: v1.20260808.1 (2026-08-08, 00:55 UTC), badged Latest by GitHub and carrying no pre-release badge; the release Atom feed confirms the absolute timestamp, and the workerd npm publish of 1.20260808.1 followed roughly five minutes later.

repos.name: vercel/ai
repos.description: Apache-2.0 licensed TypeScript monorepo for the AI SDK, Vercel's toolkit for building AI-powered applications, providing a unified generation, streaming, structured-output, tool-calling and agent interface over many model providers, together with framework bindings for React, Next.js, Svelte and Vue. It publishes the core ai package alongside a large family of @ai-sdk/* provider and utility packages, and cuts tagged GitHub releases per package many times a day. In scope for the Vercel Open Source program on HackerOne, which lists https://github.com/vercel/ai as a SOURCE_CODE asset with eligible_for_bounty=true, eligible_for_submission=true and critical maximum severity, and whose instruction reads "Please assign this to any project involving the ai-sdk repo. This is considered tier 1" — the program's highest priority band, so awards are not subject to the reduced Tier 2 rate. The material caveats are procedural rather than scope-related: every report needs a zip proof-of-concept artifact that reproduces on a stable release, and issues that exist only in canary or release-candidate builds and are superseded by a stable version are out of scope. Latest stable release: @ai-sdk/xai@4.0.33 (2026-08-07, 23:50 UTC), the tag GitHub badges Latest, with the core package's ai@7.0.58 release cut four minutes earlier at 23:46 UTC; both are stable, and no pre-release tag in this repository is newer.

repos.name: vercel/turborepo
repos.description: MIT licensed high-performance build system for JavaScript and TypeScript monorepos, written in Rust, providing content-addressed local and remote caching, task graph scheduling with automatic parallelism, incremental rebuilds that skip unchanged work, and code generation; it ships as the turbo npm package with prebuilt native binaries per platform and is used to orchestrate builds across large workspaces. In scope for the Vercel Open Source program on HackerOne, which lists https://github.com/vercel/turborepo as a SOURCE_CODE asset with eligible_for_bounty=true, eligible_for_submission=true and critical maximum severity, and whose instruction reads "Please assign this to any project involving the turborepo repo. This is considered tier 1", placing it in the program's highest priority band rather than the reduced-rate Tier 2. The material caveats are that a zip proof-of-concept artifact reproducible on a stable release is mandatory, and that canary-only issues later superseded by a stable version are out of scope — relevant here because this repository publishes a steady canary channel alongside its stable line. Latest stable release: v2.10.9 (2026-08-07, 20:56 UTC), badged Latest by GitHub, with the intervening v2.10.9-canary.1 tag (2026-08-05) excluded as a pre-release; the turbo npm publish of 2.10.9 trailed the GitHub release by about the same minute.
